semantics_represented_by_current_code: Version 1 policies, validated exact subsystem identity, and exact scope precedence entity+subsystem > entity > subsystem > global.
Admission resolves the actual owner of an existing Pending work; adapter binds to one FlowRuntime lineage on successful admission; duplicate and foreign/missing/non-Pending work fail closed.

Staging replaces the single pending policy. Boundary application checks all admitted work; Pending/Active/Suspended blocks, missing/despawned bound work fails closed, and success affects future admissions only.
Current admit is post-creation: it does not freeze policy before provider sampling/work creation and is not the C20 borrowing permit.

exact_contract_signatures: impl FidelityAdapter { pub fn prepare_admission<'a>(&'a mut self, flow: &FlowRuntime, owner: EntityId, subsystem: &str) -> Result<FidelityAdmissionPermit<'a>, FidelityError>; }

impl<'a> FidelityAdmissionPermit<'a> { pub fn decision(&self) -> FidelityDecision; pub fn bind(self, flow: &FlowRuntime, work: WorkId, expected: SimDuration) -> Result<FidelityDecision, (Self, FidelityError)>; }
requirements: Permit mutably borrows adapter across real work creation/binding so staging/application cannot change the frozen decision.
Validate actual actor/runtime lineage before resolving; bind one actual Pending work only when owner, lineage and original duration match.
Failures do not mutate adapter or Flow; where specified they return the permit for retry. Adapter runtime lineage binds only on successful bind.
Permit and its owner/runtime/decision fields are private, non-Clone/non-serialized and excluded from seed/event/checkpoint bytes.
Existing admit remains compatible and retains its test coverage.
later_frozen_permit_not_current_export.visibility: The permit is a later experimental API addition, not among current source declarations. Calibration can use it across crates only after coordinator-approved DES experimental export; keep provider/bridge state crate-private in calibration and preserve DES-to-calibration dependency prohibition.

compatibility_and_api_findings.finding: No current external fidelity API exists because lib.rs declares private mod fidelity; ADR-0007 proposes pub mod fidelity but explicitly says no source export is authorized by the ADR alone.
compatibility_and_api_findings.disposition: Conditional acceptance of the API shape only after the coordinator records exact names/signatures, independent objections and dispositions, compatibility review, and acceptance. Do not treat this read-only review as authorization.

compatibility_and_api_findings.finding: Existing fidelity_mode_c21.rs and fidelity_lineage_v1.rs path-include fidelity.rs into external integration-test crates and rely on the cfg(test)-only FidelityAdapter::clone snapshot. Promoting those tests to production module imports before moving them in-crate would lose their test-only Clone context and fail to compile.
compatibility_and_api_findings.disposition: Port mode tests into an in-crate test module first, then port lineage tests and remove the final path-included copy; reconcile original test cases/oracles before exporting the module. Do not enable production Clone or weaken snapshots.

compatibility_and_api_findings.finding: FlowRuntime::actor(&self, id: EntityId) -> Result<(), FlowError> exists in flow.rs but is private to that module. The C20 permit contract calls for crate-private actor validation so sibling fidelity code can validate a real actor. FlowRuntimeIdentity is already public and re-exported; its token representation/constructor remain opaque by design.
compatibility_and_api_findings.disposition: A crate-private-only validator/access adjustment may be needed when permit implementation starts. Preserve no new public actor helper/signature and no external world mutation. Do this only after path-included external tests are removed. Preserve the existing public FlowRuntimeIdentity type and FlowRuntime::identity method exactly; do not narrow/reclassify them or export token representation/constructor/serialization.

compatibility_and_api_findings.finding: The current types use existing stable Rust constructs and existing thiserror/types dependencies; proposal introduces no required DES dependency or DES-to-calibration edge. Fidelity adapter state is process-local and has no portable serialization promise.
compatibility_and_api_findings.disposition: Retain default DES Rust 1.76 compatibility. Calibration optional flow feature remains a separate later Rust 1.88 gate with actual production DES/ABM dependencies; canonical Rust 1.99 tests/clippy/fmt and production-feature compile are still required by ADR-0007. No check was run in this review.

review_disposition.architecture_objection: No objection to the conditional experimental API shape described by ADR-0007 and the frozen C20 contract, provided the staged test-port/export/permit order and visibility constraints above are preserved.
review_disposition.implementation_acceptance: Not granted. Current module remains private; exact exports, test migration, permit implementation, production calibration integration, toolchain gates and hosted/native evidence remain open.
review_disposition.evidence_scope: Read only fidelity.rs, DES lib.rs, ADR-0007, c20-admission-bridge-v1 and c2-execution-admission-v1 at observed HEAD. No edits, tests, builds, API publication or runtime qualification.
review_disposition.existing_public_api_preservation: No proposed restriction narrows an already-public API: FlowRuntimeIdentity and FlowRuntime::identity are public today. The recommendation is only to preserve their existing opaque behavior and keep future actor validation crate-private.
